QuestionStmt.S:
Standard potential ($E^\circ$) of $\mathrm{Zn_{(aq)}^{2+}} + 2e^- \rightarrow \mathrm{Zn_{(s)}}$ is -0.76 V. 

What is standard potential of reaction $2\mathrm{Zn_{(s)}} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{Zn_{(aq)}^{2+}} + 4e^-$?

Solution.S:
Given reduction half-reaction:
$$\mathrm{Zn^{2+}} + 2e^- \rightarrow \mathrm{Zn}, \quad E^\circ = -0.76 \text{ V}$$

The oxidation half-reaction (reverse) is:
$$\mathrm{Zn} \rightarrow \mathrm{Zn^{2+}} + 2e^-$$

For the reverse reaction, $E^\circ$ changes sign: $E^\circ = +0.76$ V.

The required reaction is simply twice the oxidation half-reaction:
$$2\mathrm{Zn} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{Zn^{2+}} + 4e^-$$

Standard potential is an intensive property; it does not depend on the number of electrons or stoichiometric coefficients. Therefore, $E^\circ$ remains $+0.76$ V.

Thus the correct option is D: +0.76 V.
